youtube.baslik: Can a tone in a dead cochlear region still be heard? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: In a cochlear dead region, the inner hair cells or the nerve fibers connected to them do not work. A loud enough tone can be detected by inner hair cells in the healthy neighboring region; this is called off-frequency listening. Patients often hear this tone as noisy, distorted or at a different pitch; the measured threshold belongs to the neighboring region, so the audiogram does not reveal a dead region by itself.
